header: Date: 2026-06-17 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~56m | Attendees: Redwood AE/SE + CedarBridge ML/Infra/Product/Sec | Meeting purpose: Scope POC timeline, access requirements, success criteria and exec readout plan
summary: Kickoff scoping focused on a 6-week POC: access & data steps this week, core benchmarking in week 2-4, midpoint review at week 3, and exec readout at week 6. Main success criteria: 99p latency target, cost-per-1k-tokens, and functional extraction accuracy. Identified VPC peering, S3 access, and KMS as primary gating items.
topics: POC timeline, access gating (VPC/S3/KMS), workload sizing, benchmark metrics (p50/p95/p99, throughput, token cost), rollbacks & fallback model plan, exec readout deliverables, security/compliance checklist
transcript:
[00:00] Evan (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time today. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Anita: Anita Rao here, head of ML at CedarBridge.
[00:09] Tom: Tom Breuer, infra.
[00:11] Priya: Priya Menon, product.
[00:12] Samir: Samir here, security.
[00:14] Maya (Redwood SE): Maya from Redwood, hi all.
[00:16] Evan: Cool. So goal today is to map the POC journey — what we need to get started (access), the bench plan, mid-point checkpoints and the exec readout format. We'll try to keep to 45-60 minutes.
[00:30] Anita: Sounds good. We're trying to validate two main things: 1) can we hit sub-200ms tail latency for our snippet-generation workload with a 1k token context and 2) the per-unit cost versus our current hosted provider. Also we need data residency notes, obviously.
[00:45] Maya: Good — those are measurable. For latency, we should capture p50, p95, p99 and cold-start behavior. For cost, we'll give tokenized cost numbers and batching tradeoffs. A quick question — are you planning to use Redwood Hosted or Dedicated for the POC?
[01:02] Anita: Ideally Dedicated for throughput parity but we might start hosted if getting infra access takes too long. We want a realistic run for production so Dedicated preferred.
[01:15] Evan: Noted. Dedicated has reserved capacity so it's the closest analog. We can spin up a small dedicated pool for the POC — we'll suggest GPU type in the runbook.
[01:30] Tom: On infra gating, we have strict VPC peering policies and need approval for outbound egress. We'll need a minimal set of IP/CIDR ranges for your cluster and a bastion for SSH. We also need S3 access pattern for the eval dataset.
[01:46] Maya: For VPC we'll ask for a single peering CIDR and one SSH bastion with a short-lived key. For the S3 dataset we just need read-only role and a sample of ~50k documents initially. If you have full PHI concerns we'll accept a sanitized subset — we can run the first benchmarks on synthetic or scrubbed data.
[02:10] Samir: Security: KMS? We require customer-managed KMS and audit logs. Does Redwood support external KMS/HSM?
[02:18] Evan: Yes, Redwood Private / Dedicated supports customer KMS integrations. We'll share the KMS options in the security packet. Note — sometimes our internal transcript shows K M S spelled differently, sorry.
[02:32] Priya: Timeline-wise what are we looking at? 4 weeks? 6 weeks?
[02:36] Maya: Our recommended footprint is 6 weeks: week 0 — kickoff & access; week 1 — baseline ingestion & small-scale bench; weeks 2–3 — full-scale benchmarks and tuning; week 4 — stabilization and runbook consolidation; week 5 — mid-point review/dry run; week 6 — exec readout and handoff. But we can compress if you have tighter timelines.
[02:58] Anita: 6 weeks is fine. We want a mid-point session to catch regressions early and an exec-ready slide pack.
[03:06] Evan: Great. Let's detail success criteria so everyone is aligned. Maya?
[03:11] Maya: Success criteria proposal: (A) Latency: p99 under 350ms for 1k context on production-like load, p50 under 120ms. (B) Throughput: sustain 80–120 qps with <5% error rate. (C) Quality: extraction F1 >= 0.88 on our test prompts. (D) Cost: tokenized cost <= your target (you shared a rough $0.08 per 1k tokens target earlier). (E) Ops: safe fallbacks and SLA playbook documented.
[03:48] Anita: F1 0.88 is good. The cost target was more like $0.06 but we'll see tradeoffs with latency.
[03:56] Evan: We'll model multiple configurations (quantized vs fp16, batching windows) and show unit economics for each.
[04:05] Tom: For the benchmarking, what's the recommended workload size?
[04:08] Maya: Start with a representative 50k sample, then scale to 250k for full run. We'll capture sequence-length distribution — you said average sequence length is ~420 tokens?
[04:20] Anita: Yes, average 420, 95th is ~1,100.
[04:25] Maya: Great — that'll affect KV cache and memory. We'll note recommended max-context and kernel choices in our suggestions.
[04:34] Priya: Exec readout — what should we present?
[04:37] Evan: Two slides: 1) Outcome vs success criteria (metrics and cost) and 2) Decision points & recommended path (go to prod on Dedicated, optimize quantization, follow deployment runbook). Add an appendix with benchmark graphs and the knob matrix.
[04:51] Priya: Ok. Also want a single-line summary for exec: "Can we deliver production performance at X cost?"
[04:58] Evan: Yes. We'll craft the one-liner.
[05:02] Tom: Access details — how do we provision credentials?
[05:05] Maya: We'll use short-lived IAM roles for S3 and a restricted SSH key for the bastion. For Dedicated / Private we need service account, peering details, and a minimal CIDR list. We'll send a checklist doc.
[05:20] Evan: We'll attach the checklist and the POC runbook in the follow-up. Links in chat: (runbook v1) https://redwood.example/runbook/CB-poc-v1 and (benchmark template) https://sheets.example/CB-bench-template — these are placeholders, will share final links after call.
[05:40] Anita: Can we do a quick run of failure scenarios? Say if load spikes or model fallback triggers — how does Redwood handle graceful degradation?
[05:48] Maya: We have routing policies — we can fall back to a cheaper model variant, route to a different region, or degrade to cached completions. We'll include a default fallback policy in the runbook. There is also a queue backpressure setting to protect latency SLOs.
[06:06] Samir: On audit and logging — we need request/response logs redacted, token-level cost telemetry, and immutable audit logs for compliance review.
[06:15] Evan: Got it. We'll surface token-level cost and provide guidance for redaction toggles. For immutable logs we can run through Dedicated / Private options that push logs to your SIEM via secure forwarder.
[06:28] Tom: Any recommended GPU types? We use A100s in prod but open to alternatives for the POC.
[06:34] Maya: For 1k context and the model size you described (13B-ish), an A100 or H100-equivalent is ideal. If you want to simulate cost parity, we can run a smaller cluster of 80–100% utilization on T4 for a cheaper run but results won't map 1:1. We'll document delta in the benchmark sheet.
[06:57] Anita: We also need to validate cold-starts when KV cache is primed vs cold — can you test both?
[07:03] Maya: Absolutely. We'll include cold/warm-start scenarios and show p99 differences.
[07:10] Priya: On governance, do you have SOC2 and ISO certs we can show?
[07:14] Evan: Yes — we'll attach current certs and the vendor security questionnaire.
[07:20] Samir: Also clarify data retention policies for logs and models — we need 30 day minima for logs and no model snapshotting of customer data.
[07:29] Maya: Redwood's default retention is 30 days for operational logs; we can configure retention for dedicated setups. And we don't snapshot or train on customer data unless explicitly opted in. We'll put that in writing in the security packet.
[07:45] Tom: Back to milestones: can you restate the week-by-week gates so I can sync with infra?
[07:50] Evan: Sure. Week 0 — kickoff & access: VPC peering, S3 role, KMS options confirmed. Week 1 — baseline ingest & smoke tests at small scale. Week 2 — scale benchmarks and start tuning. Week 3 — midpoint review; if metrics meet thresholds, move to stabilization. Week 4 — stabilization & ops runbook. Week 5 — final runs & dry-run readout. Week 6 — exec readout and handoff.
[08:27] Anita: Midpoint review — what artifacts do you expect from us?
[08:31] Maya: We'll want a small exec-ready table: pass/fail on each success criterion, a short note on mitigations, and the runbook issues list. We'll present a graph pack and an appendix with raw bench outputs.
[08:45] Priya: For the exec readout who should attend from Redwood?
[08:48] Evan: AE + SE + PM, and optionally a reliability engineer if we hit infra questions. From CedarBridge we'd want your exec sponsor and infra lead.
[08:58] Tom: Ok. On timing — can we set midpoint review for 2026-07-08? That would be ~3 weeks out.
[09:04] Anita: That works for exec calendars.
[09:07] Evan: I'll tentatively book but we'll wait for Tom to confirm access gating to lock the schedule.
[09:14] Maya: One more technical note — for KV cache priming we need representative conversational traces; if you can provide 10k warm traces we can pre-warm cache and measure best-case latencies.
[09:25] Anita: We'll extract 10k pseudonymized traces by EOD Friday, will that be enough?
[09:30] Maya: Perfect. The more realistic the traces the more accurate the bench.
[09:34] Tom: On the flip side, if we can't provision peering for legal reasons, do you have an air-gapped / on-prem packaged option?
[09:40] Evan: Yes — Redwood Private has an on-prem package but that extends timeline by 3–5 weeks for installation. We'll only recommend if peering isn't doable.
[09:49] Priya: Risk list?
[09:51] Evan: Quick risk register: 1) Access delays (VPC/KMS) — mitigated by using hosted fallback; 2) Data compliance issues — mitigated by scrubbed dataset & Private option; 3) Cost delta — mitigated by quantization and batching swaps; 4) Unexpected edge-case accuracy regressions — mitigated by additional eval buckets and rollback to baseline model.
[10:13] Samir: On the vendor questionaire — we'll send that to you after the call, expect technical Qs about key rotation, HSM certs, and incident playbooks.
[10:22] Evan: Great — we'll prioritize those in our security packet.
[10:26] Anita: Anything else?
[10:28] Evan: Let's recap next steps and owners.
[10:31] Evan: Evan - send runbook, bench template, security packet (includes SOC2/ISO and KMS options) by 2026-06-19.
[10:40] Maya: Maya - sample inference configs, cold/warm test list, and KV priming instructions by 2026-06-21.
[10:46] Tom: Tom - VPC peering details and S3 role by 2026-06-22.
[10:50] Samir: Samir - return vendor questionnaire and retention policy notes by 2026-06-24.
[10:55] Priya: Priya - draft exec bullets by 2026-07-20.
[11:00] Anita: We'll share the 10k pseudonymized traces by Friday.
[11:04] Evan: Perfect. We'll hold mid-point review tentatively 2026-07-08 and exec dry run 2026-07-29.
[11:12] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with links and the checklist.
[11:18] Anita: Thanks all.
[11:20] Evan: End.

Notes: transcription has occasional mis-hearings (e.g., redwood sometimes shown as "red wood" in older logs). Some proper nouns may be slightly off in the auto-transcript.
